title: Throughput cost sweeper: batching / cache / qconfig notes (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working memo describing a practical "throughput cost sweeper" approach: a compact set of batch / cache / quantization (qconfig) candidate settings, the columns we should include in the cost/quality spreadsheet, and an execution plan to validate and roll out the best combos. Aim: give SRE/Product/Applied-ML a reproducible checklist to run sweeps and confidently recommend safe default profiles for hosted and dedicated customers.

Context and high-level constraints:
- Target customers: mid-to-high QPS text generation and chat workloads (1–500 req/s per route in hosted, 100–5k req/s aggregated for Dedicated pools).
- Latency SLOs we commonly care about: p95 <= 200ms (low-latency features), p95 <= 600ms (interactive chat), no-SLO background batch (embeddings).
- Typical sequence lengths: short (<=32 tokens), medium (64–256 tokens), long (>=512 tokens).
- Hardware profiles: A100-80GB class (high mem), H100-like (fast kernel), T4/RTX class (cost-sensitive).
- Quality sensitivity: Some customers cannot tolerate >1.5% drop in top-level metric (ROUGE/embedding cosine).

Sweep design and spreadsheet schema (required columns):
We want a single canonical spreadsheet (CSV-friendly) for automated ingestion. Columns (literal names to use):
- model
- model_variant (float32 | int8 | int4 | mixed8_4 | gptq-4-bit)
- hardware
- workload_profile (short|medium|long|mixed)
- sim_qps (requests_per_second)
- avg_seq_len_tokens
- batch_max_tokens (max tokens accumulated before dispatch)
- batch_max_examples (max explicit examples per batch)
- batch_timeout_ms (batch coalesce timeout)
- continuous_batching (true|false)
- kv_prefix_cache (none|local|shared)
- cache_key_scheme (prefix-only|prefix+user|full-input-hash)
- cache_ttl_s
- cache_max_entries
- qconfig_notes (short free text)
- p50_latency_ms
- p95_latency_ms
- tail_latency_ms (p99)
- throughput_tokens_per_sec
- gpu_util_percent
- requests_per_sec_served
- cost_usd_per_million_tokens
- quality_delta_pct (vs baseline float32, positive=better, negative=regression)
- notes

Spreadsheet helper formula examples (put into adjacent 'calc' column or documented sheet):
- tokens_per_hour = throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600
- cost_usd_per_million_tokens = (runtime_cost_usd_per_hour / tokens_per_hour) * 1_000_000
  - runtime_cost_usd_per_hour should be computed consistently per hardware pool (include amortized infra & pod overheads).
- relative_cost_vs_baseline = cost_usd_per_million_tokens / baseline_cost_usd_per_million_tokens
- expected_savings_pct = 1 - relative_cost_vs_baseline
- deploy_safety_flag = (p95_latency_ms <= target_p95 AND quality_delta_pct >= -1.5) ? "safe" : "unsafe"

Recommended candidate settings (start here, then sweep +- neighbors):
1) Low-latency interactive (p95 target <=200ms, seq len <=64)
- batch_max_examples: 4–8
- batch_max_tokens: 256–512
- batch_timeout_ms: 10–30ms
- continuous_batching: true (aggressive coalescing with small timeouts)
- kv_prefix_cache: local (per-GPU small in-memory LRU), cache_ttl_s: 30–120s, cache_key_scheme: prefix-only
- qconfig: int8 per-channel symmetric for matmuls; keep LayerNorm/softmax float32. Evaluate int8 vs mixed8_4 if accuracy sensitive.
- expected impact: modest cost reduction (10–30%) with minimal quality change; watch p95 tail in low QPS.

2) Cost-optimized throughput (batch-friendly, seq len 64–256)
- batch_max_examples: 32–128 (depending on memory)
- batch_max_tokens: 4096–16384 (cap to avoid OOM)
- batch_timeout_ms: 50–200ms (favor throughput)
- continuous_batching: true
- kv_prefix_cache: shared (cluster-wide or route-shared), cache_ttl_s: 300–3600s, cache_key_scheme: prefix+user for personalization-aware caches
- qconfig: mixed8_4 or GPTQ-4-bit for transformer weights; keep embeddings in 8-bit if you see quality regression; evaluate per-layer fallback on attention heads
- expected impact: 2x–6x tokens/sec improvement for some models, cost reduction 40–75% depending on quant and batch sizing.

3) Conservative enterprise (SLA-sensitive, >500ms allowed but strict quality)
- batch_max_examples: 8–32
- batch_max_tokens: 1024–4096
- batch_timeout_ms: 25–100ms
- continuous_batching: false or conservative true (smaller headroom)
- kv_prefix_cache: shared with strict TTL (60–300s), cache_key_scheme: prefix+user
- qconfig: int8 or mixed8_4 with aggressive per-layer validation; avoid 4-bit unless validated on customer eval set
- expected impact: 20–50% cost improvement with low risk to quality.

Cache sizing and economics:
- Simple hit-rate model: effective_token_load = incoming_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate)
- CPU/GPU inference time scales with effective_token_load; cost savings roughly proportional to (1 - cache_hit_rate) ignoring fixed pod overheads.
- Example: if average seq_len=128, QPS=50 => tokens/s=6400. 50% hit rate => effective tokens/s=3200 => ~50% downstream token compute cost reduction.
- Memory sizing: for prefix caches use per-entry size ~= avg_prefix_tokens * embedding_size_bytes + metadata. For 8k entries with 128-token prefixes and 1536-dim float16 embeddings: estimate ~8k * 128 * 1536 * 2 bytes ≈ 3.1GB (reduce with int8 or quantized cache).

Quantization operational notes:
- Quantize offline and keep both float32 and quantized variants accessible for fallback. Use progressive rollout: synthetic bench -> internal eval -> canary traffic -> cohort rollout.
- Validate on customer prompt set; compute embedding-distance delta or downstream metric. Maintain a per-model "quality budget" (e.g., -1.5% top metric max).
- Prefer per-channel symmetric int8 for matmuls, and GPTQ for 4-bit when latency/cost gains justify extra offline cost.
- Beware of attention biases: some models degrade on QKV quantization; keep attention QKV in float if regression observed.

Testing methodology and required metrics for each sweep cell:
- Warmup: run 60s warmup at target QPS before measuring.
- Measure for 5–15 minutes depending on run stability (longer for low QPS cells).
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput tokens/sec, GPU util, memory headroom, OOM events, and model quality delta on 200 representative prompts.
- Collect system traces (trace ids) and sample generations (5–10%) for qualitative review.

Runbook for adoption (short checklist):
1) Fill spreadsheet cells for candidate combos, include baseline float32 row.
2) Run sweep automated harness (link in linked_artifacts).
3) Triage any cell where p95 latency or p99 tail > 2x baseline or quality_delta_pct < -1.5.
4) For safe cells, stage as canaries on 1–5% traffic for 24h, compare production metrics and monitor error/rollback flags.
5) Gradual rollout with automated rollback if deploy_safety_flag becomes "unsafe" or error rates increase >2x baseline.

Prioritization guidance (quick):
- Start with mixed8_4 on medium-length workloads running on H100-class hardware; highest expected bang-for-buck.
- Do not apply 4-bit variants to prompt-heavy instruction-tuned models without customer evals.

Open questions / follow-ups (to address during sweep):
- Should we standardize on a small set of qconfig labels (e.g. float32, int8_pc, mixed8_4, gptq4) vs free-text? Recommendation: enforce labels for spreadsheet hygiene.
- Investigate automated cache-key entropy analysis: how often do prefixes repeat at production scale? We need a 24h sample.
- Cost accounting: confirm which infra overheads to include in runtime_cost_usd_per_hour (billing vs amortized engineering cost).

Immediate next actions (who/when):
- Priya: seed the sweep spreadsheet with baseline rows for top 12 served models (by traffic) — due 2025-03-06.
- Mateo: add automated harness config to run jobs across hardware pools and push metrics to the spreadsheet — due 2025-03-09.
- Jonas: collect 24h prefix reuse sample and estimate cache hit potential for 3 large customers — due 2025-03-09.
- Ava: consolidate results and write a short recommendation note with 1 recommended default profile per traffic-tier — due 2025-03-16.

Appendix: quick example spreadsheet row (CSV text)
model,model_variant,hardware,workload_profile,sim_qps,avg_seq_len_tokens,batch_max_tokens,batch_max_examples,batch_timeout_ms,continuous_batching,kv_prefix_cache,cache_key_scheme,cache_ttl_s,p95_latency_ms,throughput_tokens_per_sec,gpu_util_percent,cost_usd_per_million_tokens,quality_delta_pct,notes
redwood/gpt-small,float32,A100,short,50,24,8,20,true,local,prefix-only,60,120,40000,62,18.4,0.0,baseline
redwood/gpt-small,int8_pc,A100,short,50,24,24,16,15,true,local,prefix-only,60,140,64000,78,11.2,-0.2,good tradeoff

Notes on uniqueness: this memo emphasizes a sweep-driven spreadsheet schema and a short canary/runbook that is deliberately prescriptive (formulas, CSV header names, exact batch-timeout ranges) to enable a reproducible experiment pipeline. It is intentionally more execution-and-spreadsheet focused than prior high-level presets.
